title: Crispy Thai Omelette with Fish Sauce over Rice
summary: A Thai-style khai jiao: puffed, lacy-edged omelette seasoned with fish sauce and served over hot white rice. It is fast, savoury and satisfying for a dairy-free breakfast.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in fresh water according to the packet instructions or in a rice cooker until tender and fluffy, about 12–15 minutes. Keep warm.
Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, sliced spring onions, chilli and black pepper, then beat vigorously for 30–45 seconds until very foamy.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small wok or frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. A drop of egg should sizzle immediately on contact.
Pour the beaten egg into the hot oil in one go. Let it puff and crisp without stirring for 1–2 minutes, until the edges are deep golden and lacy.
Carefully flip the omelette and cook the second side for 30–60 seconds, until golden and just set in the centre. Lift out and drain briefly on kitchen paper if desired.
Divide the hot rice between bowls, place the crispy omelette on top, and finish with coriander leaves. Serve immediately while the edges are still crisp.
